name: Evolving cinematic drone: random-modulated LFO rates on WT position and two parallel, opposite-panned filters, plus a randomized granular sample layer and FX chain
goal: Build a one-key evolving cinematic drone where nothing repeats: a wavetable oscillator whose position is swept by a very slow free-running LFO whose RATE is itself nudged by a slow smooth random modulator (small amount, ~0.07), super-unison (~2.4 detune), 1 s positive-curve attack / ~4 s decay / lower sustain / 2 s release, filter 1 (resonance, keytrack, drive, filter envelope, tiny random LFO on cutoff) and a parallel 12 dB MS-20-style filter 2 driven by a second slow LFO with its own random rate modulation (~0.13), the two filters panned ~40% left/right; add a granular sample engine (triangle grains, randomized density/size/volume/pitch, LFO-scanned start position) and a touch of white noise into both filters; FX: shimmer → ping-pong tape echo (dotted 1/8) → gentle multiband compression on lows/highs, plus reverb → soft tape distortion → second reverb, mod wheel to drive.

source.title: Create Evolving Cinematic Drones In Pigments - Full Tutorial

prerequisites: Wavetable + sample/granular engines (or Web Audio PeriodicWave crossfades + AudioWorklet granular), 2 filters in parallel with pan, 2+ LFOs with free-run and random modulators routable to LFO rate
Shimmer reverb, tape/ping-pong delay, multiband compressor, reverb, tape distortion

inputs.name: note_or_chord
inputs.description: Single held note or chord (works low too)

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Use an original or free wavetable and sample; factory table/sample names are not copied.
Values are presenter's display units; adjust by ear.
Keep random modulation of LFO rates small — large amounts make motion erratic.

steps.action: Wavetable engine: pick a folded/rich table; route LFO1 (free-running, very slow) to wavetable position from a start around the table's middle.
Make LFO1's speed drift: route a slow, smooth, free-running random modulator to LFO1 rate with a small amount (~0.07) so the sweep speeds up and slows down unpredictably.
Size: super-unison with ~2.4 detune, main tune 0; no glide/legato.
Amp envelope: ~1 s attack with slightly positive curve, ~4 s decay, slightly lower sustain, ~2 s release. Second envelope similar for filter.
Filter 1: lowered cutoff with filter envelope, some resonance, keytracking (higher keys open more) and a little drive; add LFO1 to cutoff with a tiny range.

LFO2: another slow free-running LFO whose rate is modulated by a second random source (~0.13). Add filter 2 as a 12 dB low-pass with character (MS-20-like), set filters to PARALLEL, send sources to both, and let LFO2 move filter 2 cutoff. Pan filter 1 ~40% left and filter 2 ~40% right.
steps.expect: Two independently drifting filtered images L/R

steps.action: Engine 2 (granular): load an original granular-friendly sample into both filters; enable granular with random density both directions, random size, some random volume and pitch; change grain shape to triangle (smoother than the rhythmic default); scan the start position with LFO1.
Add a little white noise into both filters (no sub needed).

FX A: shimmer (bigger size) → tape echo ping-pong dotted 1/8 → multiband compression mostly taming lows (and some highs) while letting mids through. FX B: reverb (longer decay) → soft tape distortion → second reverb.
steps.expect: Wide, spacious, mid-focused drone without low build-up

steps.action: Map mod wheel to distortion drive; trim low end/clipping as needed and save.

verification: Holding one note for 30 s yields no audibly repeating cycle.
Left and right channels move differently (filters panned).
No low-end build-up after the multiband stage.
